source_validation.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.

Floor-to-floor heights: 1F ceiling_height=3.0m, 2F z_floor=3.0m/ceiling_height=3.6m, taken from the North/South elevation overall 6600mm dimension chain (3000mm lower band + 3600mm upper band), confirmed by calibrated elevation overlays (roof/ground/floor-line pixel positions matched the chain to within rounding).
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.
Interior door heights (all F1 D-N/D-S and F2 D-N/D-S doors) are assumed 2.1m: no plan or elevation drawing dimensions an interior door height.

unresolved: Pixel-to-world calibration for each plan/elevation image was supplied by the agent from the drawings' own dimension chains and outer wall faces; it was cross-checked between plan and elevation (independent chains agree to within ~1%) but not independently verified by a third source.

F1:EXT-S-WIN1 (room_wc) and F1 corridor E/W windows use dimension chains adjacent to, but not unambiguously labelled as, those specific openings; assignment is by position and is the most consistent reading found, but remains a judgment call rather than a directly labelled chain.

scope.actual_openings: only explicit built source openings are inventoried

input_view_status.note: Only this run's hash-bound direct original returns from view_image or paired elevation views are counted. Other image tools, workers and prior runs are outside this scope. A returned image is not proof of examination, complete coverage, correct interpretation or applied heights. Use supplied relevant elevations to check each floor's opening heights; do not transfer a typical height to an unexamined opening family.

room_use_review.next_action: Use-basis records saved; unresolved inferences remain explicit.
room_use_review.interpretation: Counts cover structured role_evidence only, not semantic correctness. Legacy source_refs may contain other evidence. Unknown remains a fallback when no defensible listed use fits; it is not a preferred response to ambiguity.

decision.reason: Dimension-chain arithmetic matches the currently declared z=[1.0,2.6] for all five F1 office/store/meeting windows exactly.

claims.reason: North_view.png and South_view.png (right-side chain) both show, below the F2 floor line (world z=3.0m, the drawing's 3600/3000 split), a vertical dimension chain 400/1600/1000 reading downward: 400mm from the F2 floor line to the window head, 1600mm window height, 1000mm from window sill to the ground (z=0). This is the shared family for the three F1 office windows (north wall) and the room_store/room_meeting windows (south wall), all drawn the same size. Segment index 1 (the 1600mm span) gives the window's absolute z interval directly: [1.0, 2.6].

decision.reason: Dimension-chain arithmetic matches the currently declared z=[1.5,2.4] for the F1 room_wc window exactly.

claims.reason: South_view.png left-side chain, below the F2 floor line (z=3.0m), reads 600/900/1500 downward: 600mm from the floor line to this small room_wc window's head, 900mm window height, 1500mm from sill to ground. This chain is distinct from the door beside it (the door reaches the ground directly, sill=0, matching a different visual and no dimensioned chain). Segment index 1 (900mm) gives the window's absolute z interval: [1.5, 2.4].
unresolved: The chain is positioned between the door and this window in the drawing; assignment to the window (rather than a currently-unmodelled feature of the door) is a judgment call based on the window's visibly smaller box matching a 900mm-tall opening.

decision.reason: Dimension-chain arithmetic matches the currently declared z=[1.0,2.8] for the F1 corridor east window exactly.

claims.reason: East_view.png left-side chain, below the F2 floor line (z=3.0m), reads 200/1800/1000 downward: 200mm from the floor line to the corridor window head, 1800mm window height, 1000mm from sill to ground. Segment index 1 (1800mm) gives the window's absolute z interval: [1.0, 2.8].

decision.reason: Dimension-chain arithmetic matches the currently declared z=[4.0,5.8] for all eight F2 exterior windows exactly.

claims.reason: North_view.png, South_view.png, East_view.png and West_view.png all show, above the F2 floor line (world z=3.0m) and below the roof (z=6.6m), the same vertical dimension chain 800/1800/1000 reading downward from the roof: 800mm from roof to window head, 1800mm window height, 1000mm from sill to the F2 floor line. This is a single uniform family shared by every 2F exterior window (2 meeting-room windows on North, 4 office windows on South, 1 corridor window on each of East and West), all drawn the same height though different widths. Segment index 1 (the 1800mm span, measured from the roof-anchored origin z=6.6) gives the absolute z interval: [4.0, 5.8].

decision.reason: Pixel-measured drawn door frame extent matches the currently declared z=[0,2.1] for both F1 exterior doors.

claims.reason: West_view.png and South_view.png both draw this door's frame reaching from the ground line up to a head clearly below the F2 floor line, with no separate dimensioned chain (the nearby 600/900/1500 chain on South_view.png was assigned to the adjacent small window, not this door). Measuring the calibrated overlay pixel position of the drawn door frame against the roof/ground z-anchors on both elevations places the head at z=2.1m (sill at ground, z=0), i.e. a standard 2.1m door height; the declared z=[0,2.1] matches the drawn frame extent on both elevations to within the pixel-measurement tolerance (~0.02m).
unresolved: No printed dimension labels the door height directly; the value rests on matching the drawn frame's pixel extent against the calibrated roof/ground/floor-line anchors, not a labelled chain.

current_claim_state.note: Current numerical/context consistency only; neither retained nor confirmed means drawing truth.

height_coverage.note: Coverage means a current adopted z binding, not proof that the drawing or BIM is correct. Inference and declared values do not count as located-image height evidence.
